issue_context.title: `networkctl status` truncates link speeds
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

255

### Used distribution

NixOS

### Linux kernel version used

6.8.9

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemd-networkd

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

I got a 2.5G switch, and used `networkctl status` to check the link speed. I would have expected it to show 2.5Gbps.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

It shows `Speed: 2Gbps`, rather than `Speed: 2.5Gbps`. `ethtool` properly reports `Speed: 2500Mb/s`.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Connect a 2.5Gbps  network interface to a 2.5Gbps switch.

review_comments:
I think
```
t / table[i + 1].factor / 100 % 10
```
is simpler.
We have two tables. So the dividend is 1000 or 1024, i.e. we'd need `/ 100` or `/ 102` here (ignoring rounding).
Strictly speaking, yes. But I think the formula is much easier to read with the additional parens.
